prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier judging a wine recommender. A customer
with no wine knowledge made this request:

"I am looking to try something totally new today. Do you have any wine here made by a small independent maker?"

The recommender suggested these 5 wines (described by a professional
tasting note):

Wine 1: Pinot Noir, US, $38. Tasting note: "This fascinating medium-bodied wine has a wild streak that first brings rhubarb and forest-floor aromas, then deep dark flavor nuances like mushroom, black cherry and more tangy rhubarb. It has good acidity and fine-grained tannins to support all that complexity. It offers all the complexity one looks for in a Pinot."
Wine 2: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $25. Tasting note: "Wente continues to impress with fine wines at fair price points, and this 2007 is a case in point, a high-end offering at a still reasonable price. A rich, red Cabernet Sauvignon, with Petite Verdot and Petite Sirah in here, too, it delivers intense flavors of dark, ripe plums and brown sugar, a very agreeable Cabernet that will pair well with rich red meats."
Wine 3: Red Blend, Hungary, $30. Tasting note: "This garnet-colored Bikavér blend is comprised of Kefrankos, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Sagrantino and Kadarka. It has cherry, raspberry and plum aromas and sour cherry, raspberry and smoked meat flavors. Nicely balanced, it has rounded tannins and a prolonged finish."
Wine 4: Shiraz, Australia, $17. Tasting note: "Pretty aromas of blueberries and raspberries adorn the nose, leading into a palate of mixed berries and chocolate. This wine, which is in the medium- to full-bodied category, has a silky mouthfeel, ending in a fine dusting of cocoa powder."
Wine 5: Grenache Blanc, US, $25. Tasting note: "Sourced from the Boushey Vineyard, this includes 10% Roussanne. One-third was barrel-fermented, resulting in an especially rich mouthfeel, with a lush core of melon, tangerine, pineapple, papaya and citrus flavors. It has excellent length and power."

Rate how well each wine matches the request, using this scale:
5 = matches every wish in the request
4 = matches the main wishes, misses a minor one
3 = partly matches: right kind of wine but several wishes missed, or the reverse
2 = matches only a small part of the request
1 = does not match (wrong kind of wine, or contradicts a wish)
Judge only from the information given. A wish the information cannot
confirm (for example a price that is unknown) is neither a match nor a
mismatch.

Then rate the set:
- set_relevance: how useful the 5 wines are together as an answer to the request (1-5).

Think briefly about each wine before scoring it. Answer with JSON only, in
this form:
{"wines": [{"reason": "<one sentence>", "relevance": <1-5>}, ... one per wine, in order],
 "set_relevance": <1-5>}
